content:
We all know the remnant Dargas left in our cutural landscape are source of our history & hope for the hopeless and downtrodden. Some neo puritans, though not really puritans but with agenda of political and econmic interest destroyed some of the Dargas which are historical & archeological sites.

Every village used have some Dargas which could be forefathers of the village. It is an age old tradition to make doa for their mahfirath & also introducing their forefathers to younger generations. It is also happy moment of the family, and sharing food with poor as part of the annual event. Unfortunately no such yearly event in most of the region now.

In this context, we also had many prominent Dargas all over Tamil Nadu which also reflected our history and their contribution. Among such prominent Dargas, the Seeni Appa Darga turns to be more prominent in east Ramnad, though his influence is extended beyond Madurai, thought not like Erwadi upto Kerala.

I hear many views and opinion about Seeni Appa. Some of them are:-

1. He is local sufi imam was killed during the infamous war between muslims and Portuguese at Vedalai. During the war, many muslims were killed, their houses were burned and as a result some migrated to distance areas including Alagankulam, Irumeni, etc. It seems he used give sugar (seeni) when people visit him, that is why his name is Seeni Appa. Others said his name itself Seeni, resulting Seeni is one of the popular names of early tamil muslims in the region.

2. Some says his name was Ilme Yaseen who came from Arabia along with Sultan Syed Ibrahim Badhusa of Erwadi. During the war between Pandiyan king & Syed Ibrahim, Ilme Yaseen was killed at the coast of Sundramadaiyan. Because his name is Ya seen, he is called Seeni.

3. According to S.M. Kamal, author of Tamilakathil Muslimkal, he says in the year 1301 Madurai Sultan Jamaludin, appointed his son Bahrudin Ahmad as Emissary to China. Upon serving as Ambassdor for about 4 yrs, while returning to Madurai, just two days before reaching the coast, he died in the ship. Upon reaching the coast, his companion buried him near Sundramadaiyan. Because he came back from China, they called him Seeni appa. Even in Malaysia, the malay communities used to call china as seena. In tamil also we call seena.

I seek any other opinions & views from the readers & historians. It could be in tamil. Soon I will try practice to write in Tamil. TQ

– Nather Khan Ibrahim
